info.name: Event Ledger API
info.description:
Full test collection for the Event Ledger system — Steps 1 through 12.

Each request is labelled with the step from which it becomes functional.
Run the [Steps 1-3] folder first to confirm both services are up before anything else.

Collection variables (edit in the Variables tab):
  gateway_url          — Event Gateway base URL (default: http://localhost:9090)
  account_service_url  — Account Service base URL (default: http://localhost:8081)
  test_account_id      — Shared account used across scenarios (default: acct-123)

Out-of-order demonstration:
  The three CREDIT/DEBIT events in 'POST /events' use timestamps that are NOT
  in submission order. After submitting all three, GET /events?account= must
  return them sorted by eventTimestamp (earliest first), not by arrival order.
    evt-003 → 2026-05-10 (submitted 3rd, earliest timestamp)
    evt-001 → 2026-05-15 (submitted 1st)
    evt-002 → 2026-05-16 (submitted 2nd)
  Expected listing order: evt-003, evt-001, evt-002
  Expected balance: CREDIT 150 + CREDIT 200 - DEBIT 50 = 300.00

Idempotency note:
  Account Service always returns 201 Created for transactions — including duplicates.
  The duplicate path returns the current balance unchanged without re-applying the amount.
  Gateway returns 201 for new events and 200 for duplicate eventIds.

variable.description: Account ID used across all test scenarios

item.name: [Steps 1-3] Startup Verification
item.description:
These two requests work immediately after Steps 1-3.
Both services have no custom endpoints yet, so any request returns 404.
A 404 response from Spring Boot's default error handler confirms the service is running.
The test scripts pass as long as the service responds at all.

request.description:
Available: Steps 1-3 onwards.

Sends a GET to the root path. Spring Framework 6.1 (Spring Boot 3.x) raises
NoResourceFoundException when the static resource handler finds nothing, which
GlobalExceptionHandler maps to 404. A 404 confirms the service is up.

Expected response:
{
  "error": "No endpoint found for the requested path"
}

exec: pm.test('Gateway is responding (404 confirms service is up)', function () {

item.name: Event Gateway
item.description: All Event Gateway endpoints. Organised into sub-folders by route.

item.name: POST /events — Event Submission
item.description:
Available: Step 5 onwards (Step 4 for validation errors).

Submit the requests in order to build up test data:
  1. Submit CREDIT evt-001 (timestamp: May 15)
  2. Submit DEBIT  evt-002 (timestamp: May 16)
  3. Submit CREDIT evt-003 (timestamp: May 10 — earliest, submitted LAST)
Then use the GET /events?account= request to confirm out-of-order sorting.

request.description:
Available: Step 5+. Full Gateway → Account Service flow: Step 7+.

Submits the first event. Expected response: 201 Created.
After Step 7 (real Account Service integration), status in the response body should be PROCESSED.
Before Step 7 (stubbed client), status will be PROCESSED with a hardcoded balance.

exec: pm.test('metadata is present in response', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 5+.

Submits a DEBIT event with no metadata field. Expected response: 201 Created.
metadata should be absent from the response (null fields omitted per Jackson config).

exec: pm.test('metadata is absent (null fields omitted)', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 5+.

This event is submitted THIRD but has the EARLIEST eventTimestamp (2026-05-10).
When you call GET /events?account= after this, the listing must return events in
timestamp order: evt-003 (May 10) → evt-001 (May 15) → evt-002 (May 16).

Expected balance after all three events:
  CREDIT 150 + CREDIT 200 - DEBIT 50 = 300.00 (regardless of arrival order)

exec: pm.test('eventTimestamp is May 10 (earlier than evt-001)', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 8+.

Exact same eventId as the first CREDIT submission. The Gateway detects the duplicate
before calling the Account Service and returns the original event with 200 OK.

Key difference from the first submission:
  First submission  → 201 Created  (new event)
  This submission   → 200 OK       (original event returned, Account Service not called)

The account balance must remain unchanged after this request.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 OK (not 201 — duplicate detected)', function () {
pm.test('Original event is returned unchanged', function () {

item.name: List Events for Account — Out-of-Order Sorting [Step 5+]

request.description:
Available: Step 5+.

Run this AFTER submitting evt-001, evt-002, and evt-003 in order.

Expected order in response (sorted by eventTimestamp ASC, not by arrival):
  [0] evt-003 — 2026-05-10T08:00:00Z  (submitted 3rd, earliest timestamp)
  [1] evt-001 — 2026-05-15T14:02:11Z  (submitted 1st)
  [2] evt-002 — 2026-05-16T09:30:00Z  (submitted 2nd)

If out-of-order handling is correct, evt-003 appears first despite arriving last.

exec: pm.test('Events are sorted by eventTimestamp ASC (out-of-order proof)', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 11+.

Lists all available metric names. Look for:
  - events.submitted          (custom counter — Step 11)
  - account.service.call.duration  (custom timer — Step 11)
  - jvm.memory.used, http.server.requests, etc. (built-in Micrometer metrics)

Available: Step 11+. Requires at least one POST /events call first.

Returns total event submission count across all type/status tag combinations.
The availableTags field shows which tag values have been recorded:
  tag 'status': PROCESSED, FAILED, DUPLICATE
  tag 'type':   CREDIT, DEBIT

Available: Step 11+. Requires at least one successful POST /events.

Filters the events.submitted counter to show only PROCESSED events.
Value increments on every event that the Account Service accepted successfully.

exec: pm.test('PROCESSED count is greater than 0', function () {

item.name: Account Service
item.description: All Account Service endpoints. Internal — called only by the Event Gateway in production.

item.name: POST /accounts/{accountId}/transactions
item.description:
Available: Step 6+.

Internal endpoint. In production this is called by the Gateway only.
These requests call the Account Service directly to test its logic in isolation.

Response codes:
  201 Created — transaction applied OR duplicate detected (balance unchanged for duplicate)
  400 Bad Request — unknown transaction type
  404 Not Found — GET endpoints only (account not found)

request.description:
Available: Step 6+.

Applies a CREDIT of 150.00 to acct-123. Account is created automatically on the first transaction.
Expected: 201 Created, newBalance = 150.00

exec: pm.test('Response has transactionId and newBalance', function () {
pm.test('Response has accountId and currency', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 6+.

Applies a DEBIT of 50.00 after the CREDIT above.
Expected: 201 Created, newBalance = 100.00

exec: pm.test('newBalance is 100 after CREDIT 150 - DEBIT 50', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 6+.

Applies a CREDIT with an earlier eventTimestamp than the two existing transactions.
Balance after all three: CREDIT 150 + CREDIT 200 - DEBIT 50 = 300.00.
Addition and subtraction are commutative — the result is the same regardless of arrival order.
Expected: 201 Created, newBalance = 300.00

exec: pm.test('newBalance is 300 after all three transactions', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 8+.

Same transactionId as the first CREDIT. The Account Service detects the duplicate
(existsById check) and returns the current balance without re-applying the amount.

Note: the Account Service always returns 201 Created for transactions — including duplicates.
The duplicate path is distinguished by the balance being unchanged, not by the status code.
(The Gateway returns 200 OK for duplicates; the Account Service always returns 201.)

Expected: 201 Created, balance unchanged (still 300.00 if evt-003 was also applied).

exec: pm.test('Status is 201 Created (Account Service always returns 201)', function () {

request.description:
Available: Step 6+.

After submitting all three events (CREDIT 150, DEBIT 50, CREDIT 200), expected balance: 300.00
Balance = SUM(CREDITs) - SUM(DEBITs) = (150 + 200) - 50 = 300.00
This is correct regardless of the order events were applied.

exec: pm.test('Response has accountId, balance, currency', function () {
